sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: The **Indian National Movement** and the **Gandhian Era** (1915–1947) mark the transformative phase of India's freedom struggle.
Major Gandhian movements spanned from **1915** (return of Gandhi) to **1947** (Indian Independence).
Key figures include **Mahatma Gandhi**, **Subhas Chandra Bose**, **Bhagat Singh**, **Jawaharlal Nehru**, and **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**.
Shifted the freedom struggle from elitist politics to a **mass movement** involving peasants, workers, women, and the depressed classes.
Adoption of **Satyagraha** (truth force), **Ahimsa** (non-violence), **Non-Cooperation**, and **Civil Disobedience** as political weapons.
Divided into **Moderate Phase** (1885-1905), **Extremist Phase** (1905-1919), and **Gandhian Era** (1919-1947).
High-scoring section in **UP Assistant Teacher Exam** covering exact dates, movement triggers, and treaty outcomes.
Combination of **Swadeshi** (self-reliance), **Swaraj** (self-rule), Hindu-Muslim unity, and eradication of untouchability.

items.title: 1. Philosophy of Satyagraha and Ahimsa
items.content:
• **Satyagraha:** Persistence in truth; weapon of the strong, not the weak.
• **Ahimsa:** Absolute non-injury in thought, word, and deed.
• **Means and Ends:** Gandhi emphasized that pure ends require pure means.
• **Conscience:** Appealing to the opponent's conscience through self-suffering.
• **Mnemonic:** **S**atya **A**lways **W**ins (**S**atyagraha, **A**himsa, **W**eapon of strong).

items.title: 2. Early Experiments in India (1917–1918)
items.content:
• **Champaran Satyagraha (1917):** First civil disobedience against the **Tinkathia system** (forced indigo cultivation).
• **Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918):** First hunger strike; dispute over **Plague Bonus** between mill owners and workers.
• **Kheda Satyagraha (1918):** First non-cooperation movement; peasants demanded revenue remission due to crop failure.
• **Mnemonic:** **C**hamparan **A**lways **K**eeps (**C**hamparan, **A**hmedabad, **K**heda).

items.title: 3. Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–1922)
items.content:
• **Triggers:** **Rowlatt Act**, **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre (1919)**, and **Khilafat Issue**.
• **Programmes:** Boycott of foreign goods, government schools, courts, and titles.
• **Constructive Work:** Promotion of **Khadi**, national schools, and Hindu-Muslim unity.
• **Suspended Due To:** **Chauri Chaura incident** on **February 4, 1922**, where a police station was burnt down.

items.title: 4. Civil Disobedience Movement & Salt March (1930–1934)
items.content:
• **Trigger:** Rejection of **11 Demands** by Lord Irwin and violation of the **Salt Law**.
• **Dandi March:** Started on **March 12, 1930** from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi with **78 followers**.
• **Round Table Conferences:** First (Boycotted), Second (Attended by Gandhi), Third (Boycotted).
• **Gandhi-Irwin Pact:** Signed on **March 5, 1931**; led to suspension of the movement and release of political prisoners.

items.title: 5. Quit India Movement (1942)
items.content:
• **Trigger:** Failure of the **Cripps Mission** and Japanese advance toward India.
• **Resolution Passed:** **August 8, 1942** at Gowalia Tank, Bombay.
• **Slogan:** **'Do or Die' (Karo ya Maro)** given by Mahatma Gandhi.
• **Leaderless Movement:** Immediate arrest of all top leaders led to spontaneous public uprising and underground networks.

sections.title: Important Facts and Data
rows: 'No Dalil, No Vakil, No Appeal' law.
Massacre of peaceful protestors in Amritsar.
Led to withdrawal of Non-Cooperation Movement.
Reserved seats for Depressed Classes instead of separate electorates.
First individual satyagrahi to protest against WWII involvement.

items.term: Trick 1: Chronology of Major Mass Movements (C-N-C-Q)
items.definition: Remember **C**hamparan (**1917**), **N**on-Cooperation (**1920**), **C**ivil Disobedience (**1930**), and **Q**uit India (**1942**).
First three local interventions in India: **C**hamparan (Indigo, **1917**), **A**hmedabad (Mill workers, **1918**), **K**heda (Peasants, **1918**).
Years are consecutive: **1930** (First), **1931** (Second - Gandhi attended), **1932** (Third).
Non-Cooperation -> **Chelmsford**; Civil Disobedience -> **Irwin**; Quit India -> **Linlithgow**; Independence -> **Mountbatten**.

items.term: Trick 5: INC Sessions under Gandhi's Presidency
items.definition: Gandhi presided over only **one** Congress session: **Belgaum Session** in **1924**.
Called **'Netaji'** by German soldiers in Berlin; called Gandhi **'Father of the Nation'** from Singapore radio in 1944.
Champaran (1917) was related to **indigo planters (Tinkathia system)**, whereas Kheda (1918) was related to **land revenue remission due to crop failure**.

items.term: Mistake 2: Gandhi's attendance at Round Table Conferences
items.definition: Students often think Gandhi attended all three. He attended **only the Second Round Table Conference (1931)** as the sole INC representative.

items.term: Mistake 3: Who gave the 'Do or Die' slogan
items.definition: Many attribute 'Do or Die' to Subhas Chandra Bose or Bhagat Singh, but it was given by **Mahatma Gandhi** during the Quit India speech in 1942.
Often confused with Jawaharlal Nehru. **Acharya Vinoba Bhave** was the first individual satyagrahi; Nehru was the **second**.

items.term: Mistake 5: Date of Jallianwala Bagh Massacre
items.definition: It occurred on the day of the **Baisakhi festival** on **April 13, 1919**, not on Holi or Diwali.
The Poona Pact was signed between **Mahatma Gandhi and B.R. Ambedkar** (via Madan Mohan Malaviya as Gandhi was fasting), **not** between Gandhi and Jinnah.
Mahatma Gandhi returned from South Africa on **January 9, 1915**, bringing his technique of **Satyagraha**.
First success in India (**1917**); forced the British to abolish the exploitative **Tinkathia system**.
Passed in **March 1919**, allowing detention without trial; led to nation-wide hartals and the **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre**.
Led by **Ali brothers** (Shaukat Ali and Muhammad Ali); merged with the **Non-Cooperation Movement** to ensure Hindu-Muslim unity.
Withdrawn abruptly after the **Chauri Chaura violence** on **February 4, 1922** where **22 policemen** were killed.
Formed in **1923** by **C.R. Das** and **Motilal Nehru** to enter legislative councils and obstruct British policies from within.
All-white commission sent in **1927**; met with 'Simon Go Back' slogans; **Lala Lajpat Rai** died due to police lathi charge in Lahore.
Passed at the **Lahore Session of INC in December 1929** under the presidency of **Jawaharlal Nehru**; declared **January 26, 1930** as Independence Day.
Began on **March 12, 1930**; marked the official launch of the **Civil Disobedience Movement** by breaking the salt law.
Signed on **March 5, 1931**; led to the suspension of Civil Disobedience and Gandhi's participation in the **Second Round Table Conference**.
Signed in **September 1932**; abandoned separate electorates for Dalits in exchange for increased **reserved seats**.
Passed in **1935**; introduced **provincial autonomy** and proposed an All-India Federation.
Offered by **Lord Linlithgow** in **1940**; rejected by INC, leading to **Individual Satyagraha**.
Sent in **1942** offering Dominion Status post-war; rejected by Gandhi as a **'post-dated cheque on a crashing bank'**.
Launched in **August 1942**; final major mass struggle for complete independence with the slogan **'Do or Die'**.

upscNotes.content: For the UP Assistant Teacher Exam, memorize the exact years, locations, and leaders associated with Champaran, Ahmedabad, Kheda, and Bardoli Satyagrahas.
Focus heavily on the outcomes and dates of the Round Table Conferences and the Gandhi-Irwin Pact, as examiners frequently test these sequences.
Do not confuse the Lahore Session of 1929 (Purna Swaraj) with the Karachi Session of 1931 (Fundamental Rights & National Economic Programme).
Beware of questions asking about Gandhi's role in the Cabinet Mission or Cripps Mission—he rejected both and was not a primary negotiator.

keyTakeaways: Mahatma Gandhi transformed the Indian National Movement into a broad-based mass struggle using **Satyagraha** and **Ahimsa**.
The Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-22) united Hindus and Muslims via the Khilafat issue but was called off due to the Chauri Chaura violence.
The Civil Disobedience Movement (1930) began with the historic **Dandi Salt March** and led to the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.
The **Lahore Session (1929)** under Jawaharlal Nehru declared **Purna Swaraj** as the ultimate goal of the freedom struggle.
The **Quit India Movement (1942)** was a spontaneous leaderless uprising sparked by Gandhi's **'Do or Die'** call.
Key socio-political pacts like the **Poona Pact (1932)** shaped the representation of depressed classes in independent India.
